en: The *Buddhabhāṣita-Gautamī-sūtra*, translated by the Wu-period Yuezhi Upāsaka Zhi Qian.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, the Anāthapiṇḍika Park.
At the Nīla Vihāra,
the Buddha then suffered from a wind ailment and required cow’s milk.
At that time, there was a wealthy Brāhmaṇa living not far from the city.
At that time, the Buddha sent Ānanda, saying:
"Go to the brahmin's house and beg for cow's milk.
Having received these instructions, Ānanda went and arrived at the brahmin's house.
The brahmin asked Ānanda,
"What do you seek by coming here?
Ānanda replied:
"The Tathāgata recently suffered a slight ailment from wind, and therefore he sent me to beg for cow's milk.
The brāhmaṇa said, "The cows are over there; you may milk them yourself."
Ānanda immediately went to where the herd of cows was.
There was one cow whose nature was habitually fierce and malicious, such that no one could approach her.
Ānanda then reflected to himself:
"It is not proper for me to milk the cow myself.
At that time, Śakra, knowing what Ānanda was thinking, immediately came and manifested himself in the form of a brāhmaṇa, standing beside the cow.
Ānanda went to him and requested, saying, "Brahmin,
please milk the cow for me."
He spoke to the cow, saying,
"The Tathāgata has encountered a slight ailment from wind;
give him some milk so that he may drink it."
"O Bhikṣu, you shall obtain immeasurable merit, beyond all calculation.
The Tathāgata is the Great Teacher of those above heaven and those below heaven.
You should regard all wriggling creatures with a heart of compassion, desiring to deliver them all from suffering and affliction."
The cow said, "This hand caresses my udder; how delightful it is!
Having taken away the two front teats, he has left the two rear teats for me to nourish my calf."
"My son has not yet eaten anything since this morning.
At that time, the calf was standing nearby; hearing the name of the Buddha, it immediately said to its mother:
"Give all my portion of milk to the Buddha."
The Buddha is the Great Teacher of all that is above and below heaven;
he is exceedingly difficult to encounter.
As for me, I subsist on grass and drink water, which is sufficient for my livelihood.
Why is this? Since my previous lives, I have always drunk milk as food; now that I am to be born in the body of an ox, I shall likewise drink milk.
Those who are foolish in the world are exceedingly numerous and immeasurable.

In my previous lives, because I followed the teachings of evil associates and did not believe in the Buddha's sutras, I was made to become an ox and a horse for sixteen kalpas; it is only now that I have been able to hear the name of the Buddha.
"Take my portion of food and give it all to the Buddha; fill his bowl and depart, so that in future lives I may possess wisdom and intelligence, and attain the Way as the Buddha has."
Ānanda took the milk and returned to where the Buddha was.
The Buddha asked Ānanda,
“What did that mother cow and her calf say to one another?”
Ānanda said,
“It is truly strange.
This ox was previously extremely fierce and evil, such that one could not even approach it.”
"There was a brahmin who milked for me; the cow was well-trained, and mother and child conversed together.
The Buddha said:
"Because this mother and her calf did not believe in the Buddhist scriptures in their previous lives, they fell among cattle and horses for sixteen kalpas.
Now they have attained awakening; upon hearing the name of the Buddha, they immediately conceived a heart of compassion and offered milk to the Buddha."
In a future life, that mother cow and her calf shall become śramaṇa disciples of Maitreya Buddha and attain the state of great arhats.
After the calf dies, it shall offer hanging silk banners, pennants, and canopies for me, scatter flowers, burn incense, and uphold the sūtras and precepts.
"After twenty kalpas have passed, he shall become a Buddha named Kṣīraprabha Tathāgata, who will deliver and liberate all beings. The Buddha said,
"Because the cow gave milk to the Buddha with a virtuous and wholesome mind, she has been delivered from all suffering and hardship, and shall later obtain immeasurable rewards of merit."
For these reasons, one must believe in the Buddha, read the sutras, and study the Way.
I proclaim this throughout the heavens above and the earth below, so that all may know it.
The Sūtra on the Vatsagotra Spoken by the Buddha.
